workload_or_seed: 409 live ingest_events batches followed by compact()+gc() building an SNB SF1 native store (scripts/build_snb_store.py, M4-era usage); 2,997,352 node versions, 17,369,790 edge versions
symptom: nodes_columnar full scan on the compacted store never completed in 1,400s (killed at a 1,700s timeout) vs 7.3s on a replay of the same event log into a fresh store, for identical logical content; disk also diverged (416 segment files / 1,377.4 MB vs 408 / 536.8 MB) for the same content
root_cause: segments store rows sorted by (vt_s, vid) with transaction times run-length-encoded per segment as tt_s_runs; a live ingest batch writes exactly 1 run per segment, but compact() re-sorts globally by (vt_s, vid) while each row keeps its origin tt_s, shattering the RLE from ~1 run/segment to 2,125,704 runs for 2,997,352 rows; SegmentHeader::tt_s_at was a linear reverse scan over those runs, called once per materialized row, making a full scan effectively O(rows x runs/2)

workload_or_seed: injected-crash harness (scripts/eval_durability.py), boundary torn_wal_append: a real child process SIGKILLed mid event-log append, parent process recovers and interrogates
symptom: reopening the store after a simulated power cut mid-append raised StateError instead of recovering; a routine crash became an outage requiring manual log surgery, at the one boundary (of ten injected) the pre-registered forecast had named as the likeliest real finding
root_cause: the event log's recovery path treated any parse failure at the log's tail as fatal corruption, with no allowance for the three shapes a crash mid-append can leave (unparseable bytes, a record missing its terminal newline, or a syntactically valid record whose batch_id no longer hashes to its own content) even though such a record was never fsynced as a complete unit and so was never acknowledged to any caller

workload_or_seed: CI (Python 3.11), run 34852755086, tests/test_concurrency.py::test_readers_opening_throughout_a_write_run_never_damage_the_store: three read-only opener processes looping open/close while a writer publishes twelve generations
symptom: a read-only opener raised StateError('event log .../eventlog.jsonl is not readable at offset 4076: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 13 ...') from inside Store.__init__'s unconditional clock/frontier scan of the log, landing on the writer's in-flight (not yet fsynced) final record
root_cause: EventLog.batches_from raised StateError on any JSONDecodeError at the tail of the log, correct for a cursor landing mid-record (corruption) but wrong for a torn *final* record a live writer had not finished appending; Store.__init__(read_only=True) skips _recover() by design (recovery is a writer-only act), so trim_torn_tail never ran for a reader, and the unconditional full-log scans in last_tt()/_tt_at_offset() still raised on that in-flight tail. First fix attempt tolerated any torn final record unconditionally and regressed tests/test_eval_corruption.py::test_torn_event_log_tail_is_detected_even_read_only: a corruption sweep appending garbage to a CLOSED store produces bytes indistinguishable, by framing alone, from a live writer not-yet-finished record (both unparseable, no trailing newline, run to end-of-file, starting exactly at the manifest applied offset). Corrected to require two conditions together (Store._compute_reader_torn_tail_floor): the torn record starts at/after the manifest applied event-log offset (tolerate_torn_tail_from, same value trim_torn_tail(applied_offset) uses for a writer) AND some process currently holds writer.lock (Store._writer_lock_is_held, non-blocking flock probe) — a reader never holds this lock itself, so finding it free proves nothing could still be appending. Both hold in the real race; neither holds for the corruption sweep, which stays DETECTED.
observed_in_the_wild: Observed twice in the wild, both during the xzgpu 24 h soak at 886805f (pre-fix), same StateError shape, same failure trigger (a reader's periodic handle reopen landing on the writer's in-flight tail), both recovered cleanly by the orchestrator with the store confirmed undamaged: (1) 2026-09-15T03:15:04Z, reader 6, eventlog offset 300871482, during Store.__init__ -> _seed_frontier -> batches_from(0) (1 hit in ~2,100 reader reopens over 22 h); (2) 2026-09-15T04:44:47Z, reader 5, eventlog offset 311080182, same StateError shape and same periodic-reopen trigger, ~1.5 h later. The merged fix (3a664a8: offset floor AND live writer) covers both paths; see benchmarks/longevity-v1/README.md for the full soak record.
